name: Low-Bandwidth Data Systems
region: Global (Andes, Australia, West Africa, Pacific Islands, Arctic)
summary: Information systems that function without electricity, literacy, or high infrastructure — encoding knowledge in knots, songs, beads, tallies, smoke signals, and drum languages.

claims.statement: Talking drums in West Africa transmitted messages at speeds comparable to optical telegraph, encoding tonal language in rhythmic patterns over distances exceeding 30 km
Inuit and Polynesian wayfinding systems encode navigational data in oral traditions, star patterns, and wave-swell reading without any written or electronic instruments
Low-bandwidth data principles are being rediscovered in modern contexts: mesh networks, delay-tolerant networking, and offline-first software design

evidence.source: Carrington (1949) Talking Drums of Africa, Carey Kingsgate Press; updated by Gleick (2011) The Information, Pantheon
Lewis (1972) We, the Navigators: The Ancient Art of Landfinding in the Pacific, University of Hawaii Press
MacDonald (1998) The Arctic Sky: Inuit Astronomy, Star Lore, and Legend, Royal Ontario Museum
Fall (2003) A Delay-Tolerant Network Architecture for Challenged Internets, ACM SIGCOMM 2003
Brewer et al. (2005) The Case for Technology in Developing Regions, IEEE Computer 38(6)
